newsitem.title: USA: Season's first tropical depression spins off N.C..
newsitem.headline: Season's first tropical depression spins off N.C..

text.p: The first tropical depression of the 1997 Atlantic hurricane season has formed and was spinning south-southeast of the North Carolina coast Tuesday, posing no immediate threat to land, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 11:00 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the center of the storm system was located near latitude 31.8 north and longitude 74.2 west, or about 250 miles (405 km) south-southeast of Hatteras, North Carolina.
It was moving east near 7 mph (11 kph) and a turn toward the northeast was expected in the next 24 hours. "There is no threat to land at this time," the National Hurricane Center said.

Maximum sustained winds were near 35 mph (55 kph), with higher gusts. Little change in strength was forecast during the next 24 hours, although it would take only a small increase in wind speed to achieve maximum sustained winds of 39 mph (63 kph), at which point the system would become Tropical Storm Ana.
